entries.title: Foundations
entries.answer: Foundations: What Genesys Cloud CX is, where an organization lives, and how a voice conversation is supposed to move. This track has 8 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: What Genesys Cloud CX is
entries.answer: What Genesys Cloud CX is (Foundation, 14 min): Genesys Cloud CX is a subscription contact-center platform with four nested packages, not a single feature switch.

entries.title: Core regions and satellite media
entries.answer: Core regions and satellite media (Foundation, 16 min): An organization is born in one core AWS region. Satellite regions carry media. They do not host the org.

entries.title: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing
keywords: sip, rtp, and what the trunk is doing
entries.answer: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing (Foundation, 15 min): SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols, and Genesys trunks speak both.

entries.title: What ACD is before you name a queue
keywords: what acd is before you name a queue
entries.answer: What ACD is before you name a queue (Foundation, 12 min): ACD picks an agent for a waiting interaction. The queue is the waiting line. Skills, utilization, and On Queue decide who is eligible.

entries.title: Digital conversations beside voice
entries.answer: Digital conversations beside voice (Foundation, 12 min): Voice is one media. Architect also has inbound message, email, and chat flows, and queues track those medias separately.

entries.title: Divisions, before roles get complicated
entries.answer: Divisions, before roles get complicated (Foundation, 13 min): A division groups objects inside one organization. It is not a second org, and the Home division cannot be deleted.

entries.title: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest
keywords: how to read a genesys page without inventing the rest
entries.answer: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest (Foundation, 11 min): This lab cites the Resource Center, the Developer Center, Genesys Education, and RFCs. The page wins when they differ.

entries.title: Prerequisites before the first trunk
entries.answer: Prerequisites before the first trunk (Foundation, 13 min): BYOC Cloud needs a public carrier address, an open port plan, and a real location. The org subscription has to include the telephony product you intend to use.

entries.title: Organization and licensing
entries.answer: Organization and licensing: Regions, roles, divisions, named and concurrent licenses, packages, and fair use. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Place the organization in a core region
keywords: place the organization in a core region
entries.answer: Place the organization in a core region (Core, 12 min): You do not move an org between regions as a setting. You create it in a core region and live with that login host.

entries.title: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions
keywords: roles are permission lists paired with divisions
entries.answer: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions (Core, 13 min): A role without a division grant does not open objects. An OAuth client inherits only a subset of its creator’s pairs.

entries.title: Named licenses and the concurrent peak
keywords: named licenses and the concurrent peak
entries.answer: Named licenses and the concurrent peak (Core, 12 min): Concurrent billing charges the peak of simultaneous users, and it ignores peaks shorter than 30 minutes.

entries.title: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose
keywords: pick cx 1, cx 2, cx 3, or cx 4 on purpose
entries.answer: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose (Core, 12 min): Match the package to the job. Do not buy CX 1 and then design a WFM project.

entries.title: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line
keywords: people, queues, and the 5,000 member line
entries.answer: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line (Core, 11 min): Users live in the org. Queue membership is not the same thing as a division, and it has a hard cap.

entries.title: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice
keywords: fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice
entries.answer: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice (Core, 12 min): Licenses include monthly allowances. Overage is priced on the policy page. Copying the numbers into a design doc freezes them wrong.

entries.title: A first-week admin checklist
entries.answer: A first-week admin checklist (Core, 14 min): Week one is region, divisions, roles, packages, one queue, and a published in-queue flow. Telephony can follow.

entries.title: Architect flows
entries.answer: Architect flows: Flow types, tasks, in-queue experiences, data actions, bots, secure calls, and publish. This track has 8 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: The flow types on the Architect home page
keywords: the flow types on the architect home page
entries.answer: The flow types on the Architect home page (Core, 13 min): Architect is a list of flow types. Picking the wrong tab is the first defect.

entries.title: Tasks, menus, and a way out
keywords: tasks, menus, and a way out
entries.answer: Tasks, menus, and a way out (Core, 13 min): An inbound call flow plays audio, collects input, and must transfer, hand off, or disconnect.

entries.title: In-queue flows are the hold experience
keywords: in-queue flows are the hold experience
entries.answer: In-queue flows are the hold experience (Core, 12 min): The caller is already queued. The in-queue flow is what they hear or read while ACD looks for an agent.

entries.title: Data actions and participant data
entries.answer: Data actions and participant data (Core, 12 min): A data action calls a system outside the flow. Participant data carries a value to the agent.

entries.title: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks
keywords: common modules are how you stop copying tasks
entries.answer: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks (Core, 11 min): A common module is a flow type you call from other flows. The name is still unique inside that type.

entries.title: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording
keywords: secure call flows keep digits away from the recording
entries.answer: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording (Core, 12 min): A secure flow is how a caller enters a card number without that audio being recorded or shown to the agent.

entries.title: Call a bot from the inbound flow
keywords: call a bot from the inbound flow
entries.answer: Call a bot from the inbound flow (Core, 13 min): Dialog Engine bot flows and digital bot flows are Architect flow types. The inbound flow calls them. It does not become them.

entries.title: Publish, division, and Flow Insights
entries.answer: Publish, division, and Flow Insights (Core, 12 min): A saved flow is a draft. The runtime uses the published version. Insights tell you whether anyone hit it.

entries.title: ACD routing
entries.answer: ACD routing: Standard, bullseye, preferred, predictive, and conditional routing, plus the two scoring methods. This track has 8 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Five routing methods
entries.answer: Five routing methods (Core, 12 min): Standard, predictive, bullseye, preferred agent, and conditional group routing are the methods on a queue.

entries.title: All skills, best available, or disregard
keywords: all skills, best available, or disregard
entries.answer: All skills, best available, or disregard (Core, 13 min): The evaluation method is how standard and bullseye decide that an agent “has the skills.”

entries.title: Conversation score and priority score
entries.answer: Conversation score and priority score (Core, 12 min): One priority point on conversation score is worth 60,000 milliseconds of arrival time.

entries.title: Bullseye rings widen the target
entries.answer: Bullseye rings widen the target (Core, 14 min): Up to five rings. A delay from 2 seconds to 72 hours. Up to 50 skills removed on a ring.

entries.title: Preferred agents are tried first
entries.answer: Preferred agents are tried first (Core, 13 min): A preferred agent is considered even without the required skills, and only if they are a member of the queue and On Queue.

entries.title: Predictive routing is a KPI model with a timeout
keywords: predictive routing is a kpi model with a timeout
entries.answer: Predictive routing is a KPI model with a timeout (Advanced, 14 min): Predictive routing can run for everyone, in a comparison test, or at a fixed 80/20 split you cannot edit.

entries.title: Conditional group routing borrows agents carefully
keywords: conditional group routing borrows agents carefully
entries.answer: Conditional group routing borrows agents carefully (Advanced, 12 min): A rule is a KPI plus agent availability. The other queue must be able to spare the people.

entries.title: Utilization and Not Responding
entries.answer: Utilization and Not Responding (Core, 13 min): A fully utilized agent is skipped. An agent who ignores an alert becomes Not Responding.

entries.title: Queues, skills, and wrap-up
entries.answer: Queues, skills, and wrap-up: Queue media settings, skills, wrap-up codes, callbacks, and service level. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Create the queue in a division
keywords: create the queue in a division
entries.answer: Create the queue in a division (Core, 11 min): The queue is a named waiting line in one division, with at most 5,000 members.

entries.title: Skills and proficiency are on the agent
keywords: skills and proficiency are on the agent
entries.answer: Skills and proficiency are on the agent (Core, 12 min): The queue asks for skills. The agent profile holds them. Evaluation decides whether proficiency matters.

entries.title: After call work and the system wrap-up codes
keywords: after call work and the system wrap-up codes
entries.answer: After call work and the system wrap-up codes (Core, 13 min): ACW is optional, discretionary, or time-boxed. The platform has its own codes when agents do not finish.

entries.title: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too
keywords: wrap-up codes live in divisions too
entries.answer: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too (Core, 11 min): The codes an agent sees are the codes their role can see, and Genesys wants them in the queue’s division.

entries.title: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds
keywords: service level is a percentage and a target in seconds
entries.answer: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds (Core, 11 min): Each media has a service level percentage and a target duration. That pair is what conditional routing and WFM both mean by “the goal.”

entries.title: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules
keywords: callbacks are interactions with their own rules
entries.answer: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules (Core, 12 min): A callback is queued work. It still needs a wrap-up code, and it counts as its own utilization slot.

entries.title: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap
keywords: membership, on queue, and the copy trap
entries.answer: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap (Core, 11 min): A copied queue can duplicate a bullseye you did not mean to clone.

entries.title: BYOC Cloud and SIP trunks
entries.answer: BYOC Cloud and SIP trunks: Carrier and PBX trunks, RTP over the internet, Dynamic Cloud Voice, and the quick-start order. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: BYOC Cloud is your carrier, Genesys’ media
keywords: byoc cloud is your carrier, genesys’ media
entries.answer: BYOC Cloud is your carrier, Genesys’ media (Core, 12 min): You bring the carrier contract. Genesys terminates a SIP trunk on the AWS media tier. Audio is RTP on the internet.

entries.title: Carrier trunks and PBX trunks
entries.answer: Carrier trunks and PBX trunks (Core, 12 min): BYOC Carrier and BYOC PBX are the two types. Carrier has subtypes. PBX has one.

entries.title: The quick-start order
entries.answer: The quick-start order (Core, 12 min): Location, trunk, outbound route, number plan. The product on the subscription comes before all of that.

entries.title: Dynamic Cloud Voice is the current platform
keywords: dynamic cloud voice is the current platform
entries.answer: Dynamic Cloud Voice is the current platform (Advanced, 13 min): New trunks start there. Moving an old trunk means allow lists, Amazon root CAs, TLS ciphers, and a toggle.

entries.title: Number plans classify what people dial
keywords: number plans classify what people dial
entries.answer: Number plans classify what people dial (Core, 13 min): A site can hold 200 plans. DIDs do not need one for basic routing. Emergency, extension, and 988 already exist as defaults.

entries.title: Watch the trunk, not only the flow
keywords: watch the trunk, not only the flow
entries.answer: Watch the trunk, not only the flow (Core, 11 min): When audio fails and Architect Insights still shows runs, the trunk is the next object.

entries.title: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door
keywords: genesys cloud voice is the other door
entries.answer: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door (Core, 12 min): If Genesys is the carrier, you buy numbers in a region that offers voice, and emergency is part of that product story rather than your trunk.

entries.title: The Edge and BYOC Premises
entries.answer: The Edge and BYOC Premises: Premises Edges, Edge groups, phone trunks, sites, and what happens when the local Edge is down. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: The premises Edge is the local media hop
keywords: the premises edge is the local media hop
entries.answer: The premises Edge is the local media hop (Core, 12 min): BYOC Premises puts an Edge on your network. Phones and trunks registered there do not need a public address the way BYOC Cloud does.

entries.title: Local site routing stays home until it cannot
keywords: local site routing stays home until it cannot
entries.answer: Local site routing stays home until it cannot (Core, 12 min): Genesys uses Edges in the same site when it can. Another site is the exception.

entries.title: Phone trunks, WebRTC, and inherit
entries.answer: Phone trunks, WebRTC, and inherit (Core, 11 min): WebRTC and SIP phones are phone trunks on the Edge group. Inherit is the default you should verify.

entries.title: When the local Edge is offline
keywords: when the local edge is offline
entries.answer: When the local Edge is offline (Core, 12 min): The documented failover is another site, if that site actually has the resource.

entries.title: Choose Cloud, Premises, or both
entries.answer: Choose Cloud, Premises, or both (Core, 12 min): Use premises when the phones and the carrier are on your network. Use cloud when they are not. Use both only where each number has an owner.

entries.title: A browser phone is still a network endpoint
keywords: a browser phone is still a network endpoint
entries.answer: A browser phone is still a network endpoint (Core, 11 min): WebRTC removes the desk set. It does not remove media engineering.

entries.title: Premises turn-up checklist
entries.answer: Premises turn-up checklist (Core, 12 min): Group, inherit, site, trunk, failover test, emergency owner.

entries.title: Numbers and emergency calling
entries.answer: Numbers and emergency calling: E.164, emergency classifications, BYOC warnings, and Genesys Cloud Voice coverage. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Name the emergency owner before the DID
keywords: name the emergency owner before the did
entries.answer: Name the emergency owner before the DID (Core, 12 min): Genesys is not responsible for emergency calls that ride a BYOC trunk. That sentence belongs in the design, not in the postmortem.

entries.title: Emergency is a classification and a route
keywords: emergency is a classification and a route
entries.answer: Emergency is a classification and a route (Core, 12 min): The default Emergency plan matches 911 and 933 in the US and Canada, and 142 in Switzerland. It still needs a route.

entries.title: The location is a physical place
keywords: the location is a physical place
entries.answer: The location is a physical place (Core, 11 min): The quick start adds a location because services, including emergency, need a real site.

entries.title: Voice coverage is a table, not a promise
keywords: voice coverage is a table, not a promise
entries.answer: Voice coverage is a table, not a promise (Advanced, 12 min): Country rows decide DID, toll-free, domestic, and international. FedRAMP and the sovereign region add harder edges.

entries.title: Normalize toward E.164 on purpose
entries.answer: Normalize toward E.164 on purpose (Core, 11 min): Intra-country and inter-country plans normalize. Digit-length extensions and E.164 lists do not.

entries.title: Test emergency like a change, not like a demo
keywords: test emergency like a change, not like a demo
entries.answer: Test emergency like a change, not like a demo (Core, 12 min): A live emergency test is a carrier and public-safety conversation. The call simulator is the part you can do alone.

entries.title: Workforce management
entries.answer: Workforce management: Business units, forecasts, schedules, adherence, and time off. WFM is a CX 3 capability. This track has 9 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them
keywords: wem is a set of products, and wfm is one of them
entries.answer: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them (Core, 12 min): Recording, screen recording, quality, performance, speech and text analytics, and workforce management are the WEM list.

entries.title: Business units and management units
entries.answer: Business units and management units (Core, 12 min): A business unit is the planning container. A management unit is the group of agents you actually schedule.

entries.title: Service goal templates are the planning target
keywords: service goal templates are the planning target
entries.answer: Service goal templates are the planning target (Core, 11 min): The queue’s service level and the WFM template should describe the same promise.

entries.title: Schedules are the plan agents work
keywords: schedules are the plan agents work
entries.answer: Schedules are the plan agents work (Core, 11 min): A schedule is built from the management unit, the goals, and activity codes. It is not a routing method.

entries.title: Intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor
keywords: intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor
entries.answer: Intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor (Core, 12 min): Adherence is the gap between the activity you scheduled and the status the agent is actually in.

entries.title: Time off is a schedule change with a rule
keywords: time off is a schedule change with a rule
entries.answer: Time off is a schedule change with a rule (Core, 11 min): Time-off requests are part of WFM. An approved request that nobody reflects on the schedule is a rumor.

entries.title: The workforce certification is a named exam
keywords: the workforce certification is a named exam
entries.answer: The workforce certification is a named exam (Core, 10 min): The catalog lists a Workforce Management specialist certification and a preparation course. It does not list a code this lab is willing to invent.

entries.title: A forecast has a short view and a long view
keywords: a forecast has a short view and a long view
entries.answer: A forecast has a short view and a long view (Advanced, 13 min): Short-term data can build a schedule. The long-term view is for seasonality and does not generate one.

entries.title: Generate one schedule from a forecast that covers it
keywords: generate one schedule from a forecast that covers it
entries.answer: Generate one schedule from a forecast that covers it (Advanced, 13 min): The schedule period has to sit inside the short-term forecast, and a business unit generates one schedule at a time.

entries.title: Quality and recording
entries.answer: Quality and recording: Evaluation forms, calibration, coaching, recording policies, and the prerequisites for AI scoring. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Quality management evaluates the conversation
entries.answer: Quality management evaluates the conversation (Core, 11 min): QM records and scores interactions, and it can coach. It is not the schedule.

entries.title: Forms have questions and weights
entries.answer: Forms have questions and weights (Core, 11 min): The form is the rubric. Weights decide which questions move the score.

entries.title: Recording policies choose calls and retention
keywords: recording policies choose calls and retention
entries.answer: Recording policies choose calls and retention (Core, 11 min): A policy decides which ACD calls are recorded and how long they are kept. A secure flow is a hole in a segment, not a substitute for the policy.

entries.title: Coaching and disputes close the loop
keywords: coaching and disputes close the loop
entries.answer: Coaching and disputes close the loop (Core, 11 min): A score that the agent cannot see and cannot dispute is not a quality program.

entries.title: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens
keywords: ai scoring needs sta, qm, and tokens
entries.answer: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens (Advanced, 12 min): The FAQ is blunt: AI scoring requires Speech and Text Analytics, Quality Management, and AI Experience Tokens.

entries.title: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded
keywords: retention, export, and the reason you recorded
entries.answer: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded (Advanced, 11 min): Export and AWS recording paths exist so a recording can leave the platform under a policy, not as a side copy.

entries.title: Speech and text analytics
entries.answer: Speech and text analytics: What gets transcribed, how sentiment and topics are used, and why analysis is not the same thing as the live conversation. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it
keywords: sta reads the conversation after the channel has it
entries.answer: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it (Core, 12 min): Speech and text analytics covers voice and digital interactions. It is not a second ACD.

entries.title: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with
keywords: sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with
entries.answer: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with (Core, 11 min): Sentiment scores the customer’s language. Use it as a filter, then listen.

entries.title: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary
keywords: topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary
entries.answer: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary (Core, 12 min): A program groups topics. A topic is phrases you expect to hear or read.

entries.title: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question
keywords: agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question
entries.answer: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question (Core, 11 min): Empathy detection points at calls. Calibration still decides what empathy means for your company.

entries.title: Content search is how you test the dictionary
keywords: content search is how you test the dictionary
entries.answer: Content search is how you test the dictionary (Core, 11 min): Search the transcript before you trust a topic count.

entries.title: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks
keywords: full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks
entries.answer: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks (Advanced, 12 min): Some views wait until the interaction is complete. A lower-latency transcript path is a different API.

entries.title: Genesys AI and bots
entries.answer: Genesys AI and bots: Dialog Engine and digital bots, failure paths, Agent Copilot, tokens, and the AI exams as the catalog names them. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent
keywords: two architect bot types, plus copilot beside the agent
entries.answer: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent (Core, 12 min): A bot flow talks to the customer. Agent Copilot talks to the agent. They are different products on different pages.

entries.title: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents
keywords: dialog engine bot flows are voice and digital intents
entries.answer: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents (Core, 12 min): You build the bot in Architect, then the inbound flow calls it.

entries.title: Digital bot flows are a different call
keywords: digital bot flows are a different call
entries.answer: Digital bot flows are a different call (Core, 11 min): Message experiences use Digital Bot Flows and Call Digital Bot Flow.

entries.title: Every bot has a failure output to a queue
keywords: every bot has a failure output to a queue
entries.answer: Every bot has a failure output to a queue (Core, 11 min): No-match, timeout, and error are normal. The queue is the design.

entries.title: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction
keywords: agent copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction
entries.answer: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction (Core, 12 min): Knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, and notes. The benefit is described as surviving a blind transfer.

entries.title: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read
keywords: tokens are a published allotment, and a faq ratio you re-read
entries.answer: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read (Advanced, 12 min): The overview publishes CX 4 token counts. The STA FAQ publishes how AI scoring spends them.

entries.title: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each
keywords: the ai exams are named on the catalog, one exam each
entries.answer: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each (Core, 10 min): Two AI certifications. No invented exam codes.

entries.title: Platform APIs
entries.answer: Platform APIs: OAuth grants, client credentials limits, region hosts, and why this lab’s explorer never sends a request. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: The Developer Center is the map. This lab is not a client.
keywords: the developer center is the map. this lab is not a client.
entries.answer: The Developer Center is the map. This lab is not a client. (Core, 11 min): Read the public docs. Do not point a tutorial at a production org.

entries.title: Pick the grant that matches who the call runs as
keywords: pick the grant that matches who the call runs as
entries.answer: Pick the grant that matches who the call runs as (Core, 12 min): Client credentials, authorization code with PKCE, and SAML2 Bearer are the grants to learn. Implicit is the one leaving.

entries.title: Client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call
keywords: client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call
entries.answer: Client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call (Core, 12 min): The token is the client. The guide shows that limit on purpose.

entries.title: Implicit grant is a migration, not a new design
keywords: implicit grant is a migration, not a new design
entries.answer: Implicit grant is a migration, not a new design (Core, 11 min): The OAuth article dates the deprecation: after 25 May 2026.

entries.title: Login host and API host are a pair you look up
keywords: login host and api host are a pair you look up
entries.answer: Login host and API host are a pair you look up (Core, 12 min): US East is the pair this lab will quote in full. Other rows stay on the regions article.

entries.title: Role and division pairs are the real permission
keywords: role and division pairs are the real permission
entries.answer: Role and division pairs are the real permission (Core, 12 min): A token opens the door the role allows, in the division the pair names.

entries.title: SCIM and other directory sync still start with an OAuth client
keywords: scim and other directory sync still start with an oauth client
entries.answer: SCIM and other directory sync still start with an OAuth client (Core, 11 min): The OAuth article points SCIM at a client. The client still has roles and a grant.

entries.title: AppFoundry and CRM
entries.answer: AppFoundry and CRM: The marketplace, the documented Salesforce and Zendesk embeds, and OAuth migrations that do not invent other CRMs. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: AppFoundry is the marketplace, not a feature you assume is installed
keywords: appfoundry is the marketplace, not a feature you assume is installed
entries.answer: AppFoundry is the marketplace, not a feature you assume is installed (Core, 11 min): An app is present only after someone installs it into the org.

entries.title: Genesys Cloud for Salesforce is a documented embed
keywords: genesys cloud for salesforce is a documented embed
entries.answer: Genesys Cloud for Salesforce is a documented embed (Core, 12 min): Screen pop, click-to-dial, logging, and the assist features that page names.

entries.title: Salesforce data actions move to OAuth client credentials
keywords: salesforce data actions move to oauth client credentials
entries.answer: Salesforce data actions move to OAuth client credentials (Core, 12 min): Consumer key, secret, and My Domain URL. The request body of the action stays.

entries.title: Zendesk has its own about page, with a similar embed idea
keywords: zendesk has its own about page, with a similar embed idea
entries.answer: Zendesk has its own about page, with a similar embed idea (Core, 11 min): Do not copy the Salesforce field list onto Zendesk.

entries.title: Dynamics, ServiceNow, and the rest stay on the marketplace
keywords: dynamics, servicenow, and the rest stay on the marketplace
entries.answer: Dynamics, ServiceNow, and the rest stay on the marketplace (Core, 11 min): No invented feature lists for CRMs this lab did not open.

entries.title: A CRM failure is not an ACD failure
keywords: a crm failure is not an acd failure
entries.answer: A CRM failure is not an ACD failure (Core, 11 min): Screen pop can die while the queue is healthy.

entries.title: Migration
entries.answer: Migration: Engage, PureConnect, and Cisco UCCE move by rebuilding Architect flows and queues. This is a learning bridge, not a converter. This track has 8 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Nothing imports your old routing by magic
keywords: nothing imports your old routing by magic
entries.answer: Nothing imports your old routing by magic (Core, 12 min): You rebuild flows, queues, and trunks. You do not flip a converter this lab has not found.

entries.title: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues
keywords: engage and pureconnect become flows and queues
entries.answer: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues (Core, 12 min): Strategies, IRDs, and handlers are read as behavior, then redrawn.

entries.title: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio
keywords: ivr becomes architect tasks, menus, and audio
entries.answer: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio (Core, 12 min): CVP, UCCX prompts, and Engage voice all become the same kind of flow.

entries.title: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues
keywords: ucce skill groups and precision queues are not genesys queues
entries.answer: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues (Core, 13 min): Membership, skills, and bullseye are three ideas you reassemble.

entries.title: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule
keywords: uccx is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule
entries.answer: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule (Core, 11 min): Scripts, CSQs, and the Finesse desktop do not move as files.

entries.title: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster.
keywords: cucm stays. byoc is the door, not a replacement cluster.
entries.answer: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster. (Core, 12 min): A dial plan and a trunk are Genesys number plans and a BYOC trunk. CUCM is still yours.

entries.title: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize
keywords: webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize
entries.answer: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize (Core, 10 min): Use Cisco’s product pages. Do not cite a Webex help URL this lab did not confirm.

entries.title: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people
keywords: cut over one number, then the queue, then the people
entries.answer: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people (Core, 12 min): A weekend big-bang is how untested emergency routes meet a full staff.

entries.title: Ecosystem
entries.answer: Ecosystem: How the tracks fit, how to read certifications, and what this lab refuses to invent. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: The conversation crosses a short list of systems
keywords: the conversation crosses a short list of systems
entries.answer: The conversation crosses a short list of systems (Foundation, 12 min): Carrier, trunk or Edge, Architect, queue, agent, then the systems beside the agent.

entries.title: WFM, QM, E911, analytics, CRM, and bots are sisters
keywords: wfm, qm, e911, analytics, crm, and bots are sisters
entries.answer: WFM, QM, E911, analytics, CRM, and bots are sisters (Core, 12 min): Each sister has a track and a page. None of them is a setting on the queue tab alone.

entries.title: The Cisco bridge is a translation, with both citations showing
keywords: the cisco bridge is a translation, with both citations showing
entries.answer: The Cisco bridge is a translation, with both citations showing (Core, 11 min): UCCE, UCCX, CUCM, and Webex are named so a Cisco engineer can find the door.

entries.title: Read the catalog by name, then the announcement
keywords: read the catalog by name, then the announcement
entries.answer: Read the catalog by name, then the announcement (Core, 11 min): GC-GCP and GC-GCD are catalog codes. Specialist rows are names. AI rows are two exams.

entries.title: Interview answers cite a page, not a vibe
keywords: interview answers cite a page, not a vibe
entries.answer: Interview answers cite a page, not a vibe (Core, 11 min): The drill in this lab is a set of questions with a model answer and a link.

entries.title: What this lab will not invent
keywords: what this lab will not invent
entries.answer: What this lab will not invent (Foundation, 10 min): Prices, unconfirmed hosts, exam codes, lifecycle dates, and CRM feature lists stay off the page.

entries.title: Predictive Engagement
entries.answer: Predictive Engagement: Website journeys, segments, action maps, Messenger, and the Journey Outcomes deprecation. This is not ACD predictive routing. This track has 7 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math
keywords: predictive engagement watches the site, not the queue math
entries.answer: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math (Core, 13 min): It predicts what a visitor is trying to do and offers a message, a chat, content, or a flow. Predictive routing is a different feature on the queue.

entries.title: Messenger tracks web messaging. The old snippet tracks web chat.
keywords: messenger tracks web messaging. the old snippet tracks web chat.
entries.answer: Messenger tracks web messaging. The old snippet tracks web chat. (Core, 14 min): Genesys tells Genesys Cloud CX customers to use web messaging. Leaving both snippets on the page double-counts the visit.

entries.title: A segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed
keywords: a segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed
entries.answer: A segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed (Core, 12 min): At least one condition. More conditions, fewer visitors. Conditions are not shared with the next segment.

entries.title: An action map is qualified before it is offered
keywords: an action map is qualified before it is offered
entries.answer: An action map is qualified before it is offered (Core, 14 min): Segment, visitor activity, and outcome probability are the trigger kinds. Priority breaks a tie. Web chat is the legacy action.

entries.title: Journey Outcomes have a published end date
keywords: journey outcomes have a published end date
entries.answer: Journey Outcomes have a published end date (Advanced, 14 min): Announced 18 May 2026. Planned effective date 29 June 2026. Outcome scoring is not part of the Customer Outcomes replacement.

entries.title: An Architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit
keywords: an architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit
entries.answer: An Architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit (Advanced, 12 min): Advanced orchestration is an action type. Flows that still call getJourneyOutcome need a path that does not depend on it.

entries.title: Prove the map with Live Now and the performance reports
keywords: prove the map with live now and the performance reports
entries.answer: Prove the map with Live Now and the performance reports (Core, 12 min): Visitor activity and action-map performance are the Predictive Engagement reports. Outcome columns age out with the deprecation.

entries.title: What this lab is
entries.answer: Signal Floor is a free, static operations lab for Genesys Cloud CX. It runs in the browser, stores progress locally, and does not call a live organization.

entries.title: Lucky
entries.answer: Lucky is a lifelong student and an AI enthusiast, from systems, networking, voice, and the contact center, growing into AI omni-channel agents. The copyright line on this floor is © 2026 CypherMonkeyLabs.

entries.title: Where to find Lucky
entries.answer: Three links: the website https://cyphermonkeylabs.com, the GitHub organization https://github.com/CypherMonkeyLabs, and https://linktr.ee/cypherMonkey. Contact is the website contact section https://cyphermonkeylabs.com/#contact.

entries.title: Copyright
entries.answer: The footer says © 2026 CypherMonkeyLabs. Code is MIT. Educational prose is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Genesys, Cisco, Salesforce, or Zendesk.

entries.title: Search
entries.answer: Search reads lesson titles and summaries in this browser, plus glossary lines. Nothing is sent to a server.

entries.title: Diagrams
entries.answer: The diagram atlas is a set of teaching sketches. Each caption names the limit of the drawing. The link is the source. Enlarge a picture to play, pause, or step the marker.

entries.title: Flows
entries.answer: Flows are the animated pictures from the atlas, plus sequence drawings generated with Mermaid at build time. The runtime does not load Mermaid.

entries.title: Charts
entries.answer: Charts count lessons, minutes, levels, quiz items, diagram kinds, and port-table rows from this lab. They are not Genesys production metrics.

entries.title: Cheat codes
entries.answer: Cheat codes are one-page sheets as HTML, PDF, and PNG, plus a flashcard deck and an offline zip. Each file links back to a public source instead of pasting the vendor document.

entries.title: SIP and RTP
entries.answer: SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols. TLS trunks use TCP 5061. UDP or TCP trunks commonly use 5060. Both ends must match. Media is UDP 16384-65535, opened outbound, RTP or SRTP.

entries.title: Phone signaling ports
entries.answer: Managed phones signal on TCP 8061. Unmanaged phones use TCP 5061. Phone provisioning uses TCP 443, and the phone article also lists TCP 80.

entries.title: Secure BYOC
entries.answer: Secure BYOC Cloud does not use IPsec. Use SIP TLS 1.2 and SRTP. Signaling addresses and SDP media addresses are different. Do not paste an address from this lab. Synthetic logs use RFC 5737.

entries.title: Publish versus draft
entries.answer: Save is a draft. Publish is what answers. A published Architect flow decides. A draft does not answer. The in-queue flow is the hold experience and must be published too.

entries.title: ACD evaluation
entries.answer: All-skills matching needs every required skill, then the longest idle. Preferred agents are first only if they are members and On Queue. Utilized or off-queue agents are skipped.

entries.title: Bullseye routing
entries.answer: Bullseye routing uses up to five rings. A long delay means the outer ring is still closed. A skill can drop after the ring delay.

entries.title: Conversation score
entries.answer: One conversation-score priority point is 60,000 ms. In this lab’s router, a priority of 5 beats a priority of 0 that arrived four minutes earlier.

entries.title: Predictive routing versus engagement
entries.answer: Predictive routing is the queue method. Predictive Engagement is the website product. They are not the same feature.

entries.title: BYOC
entries.answer: BYOC Cloud is your carrier and Genesys media, with no customer Edge on that path. BYOC Premises keeps phones and trunks on your Edge. Genesys Cloud Voice is the door where Genesys is the carrier.

entries.title: Emergency calling
entries.answer: On BYOC, Genesys is not the emergency provider. You classify, route, and test. A live emergency test is a carrier and public-safety conversation, not a demo.

entries.title: Workforce management
entries.answer: WFM is part of WEM and arrives with CX 3 on the overview. Short-term forecasts use interval data, up to six weeks, and can generate a schedule. Long-term forecasts use day and week data, up to two years, and cannot generate a schedule. Swapping the forecast does not move agent shifts until you reschedule.

entries.title: Quality management
entries.answer: Quality management evaluates. It does not build the schedule. A recording policy decides which calls are kept. A form decides the score. A secure flow can suppress a payment segment. It does not replace the policy.

entries.title: OAuth grants
entries.answer: Client credentials are for a service. That token cannot call /api/v2/users/me. User-facing apps use authorization code with PKCE. Token Implicit Grant is documented as deprecated after 25 May 2026. This lab’s API explorer never sends the sample.

entries.title: Journey Outcomes
entries.answer: Journey Outcomes deprecation was announced 2026-05-18, with a planned effective date of 2026-06-29, on the page this lab read. This lab has not confirmed later edits. If the page moved, the page wins.

entries.title: Certifications
entries.answer: Say the catalog names. This lab does not invent a GCX- code. GC-GCP is the professional exam. GC-GCD is the developer exam. This lab’s quiz is not Genesys’ practice exam.

entries.title: CRM embeds
entries.answer: Salesforce and Zendesk are the documented embeds named in this lab. Other CRMs stay on AppFoundry. A dead screen pop means the embed failed. The queue did not.

entries.title: Regions
entries.answer: An organization is created in one core AWS region. Satellite regions carry media and cannot host the org. This lab names only the hosts it has already checked.

entries.title: Divisions
entries.answer: A division groups objects inside one organization. It is not a second org, and the Home division cannot be deleted. A role works only in the divisions it is paired with.

entries.title: Migration
entries.answer: Rebuild the behavior. This lab has not found a converter. UCCE skill groups are membership plus skills, not one Genesys object. Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people.

entries.title: Reduced motion
entries.answer: If the device asks for reduced motion, or Settings turns reduce on, the 3D floor stays on the flat drawing and looping animations stop. Sound and reduced motion are in Settings.

entries.title: Guide Bot
entries.answer: Guide Bot is a scripted widget in this browser. It matches these notes with keywords and synonyms. It can run a short tour or a quiz and show the score. It does not invent a fact that is not in the notes. A future cloud agent can be attached by setting window.GCCX_GUIDE_ENDPOINT to an https URL that returns grounded:true plus an answer and an https source. This build does not call one unless that hook is set.

entries.title: Ecosystem
entries.answer: The Ecosystem page maps every track. WEM, recording, emergency calling, CRM, and bots sit on documented edges of Genesys Cloud CX. The glossary, certifications, and boss incidents are linked from that page.

entries.title: CX packages
entries.answer: Genesys Cloud CX is a subscription contact-center platform with four nested packages, not a single feature switch. WFM is described as arriving with CX 3 on the workforce overview.

entries.title: Digital beside voice
entries.answer: Voice is one media. Architect also has inbound message, email, and chat flows, and queues track those medias separately. Digital conversations skip the trunk and still need a flow and a queue.

entries.title: Bot flows
entries.answer: Call a bot from the inbound flow. Bind no-match, timeout, and error to a queue. A secure flow keeps payment audio out of the recording. It is not a place to store the digits.

entries.title: The Edge
entries.answer: BYOC Premises keeps phones and trunks on your Edge. Another site is failover only. The topology view can show the Edge path and a failure toggle.

entries.title: Progress
entries.answer: Progress stays in this browser. Track JSON loads when you open a track. The service worker does not prefetch every track at install.

entries.title: Skills and ACD
synonyms: how genesys cloud matches a skill request to an agent, from the acd idea through filters, rings, and direct routing
entries.answer: Skills and ACD: How Genesys Cloud matches a skill request to an agent, from the ACD idea through filters, rings, and direct routing. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: ACD is the match, and skills are one way to make it
keywords: acd is the match, and skills are one way to make it
entries.answer: ACD is the match, and skills are one way to make it (Foundation, 12 min): Wikipedia describes an ACD as a distributor. Genesys Cloud puts that job on the queue’s routing method.

entries.title: Three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback
keywords: three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback
entries.answer: Three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback (Foundation, 13 min): All skills matching, best available skills, and disregard skills do different jobs. Proficiency covers ACD skills and language skills together.

entries.title: Bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways
keywords: bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways
entries.answer: Bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways (Core, 14 min): One way adds skill-expression groups. The other removes skills. The ring count is not the same sentence on every page.

entries.title: A skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list
keywords: a skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list
entries.answer: A skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list (Core, 13 min): It works for standard and predictive routing when evaluation is All skills matching. Other methods ignore it.

entries.title: Direct routing still uses a queue
keywords: direct routing still uses a queue
entries.answer: Direct routing still uses a queue (Advanced, 13 min): The customer reaches a dedicated person. Wrap-up still exists, because the interaction is ACD.

entries.title: Preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size
keywords: preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size
entries.answer: Preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size (Advanced, 13 min): Architect’s agent-score collection supports 20 pairs unless Customer Care raises it. More than 20 fails a call flow.

entries.title: Workforce and forecasting
synonyms: forecast views, creation methods, the editor, and the short-term weeks that are allowed to build a schedule
entries.answer: Workforce and forecasting: Forecast views, creation methods, the editor, and the short-term weeks that are allowed to build a schedule. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: A forecast is a WFM plan for interactions, not a routing method
keywords: a forecast is a wfm plan for interactions, not a routing method
entries.answer: A forecast is a WFM plan for interactions, not a routing method (Foundation, 12 min): Workforce management is one WEM product. The forecast article names the metrics and the permissions.

entries.title: Short-term weeks can schedule. Long-term weeks cannot
keywords: short-term weeks can schedule. long-term weeks cannot
entries.answer: Short-term weeks can schedule. Long-term weeks cannot (Foundation, 12 min): Six weeks of intervals on one side. Up to two years of days and weeks on the other.

entries.title: Four creation methods, and a 130-week outer limit
keywords: four creation methods, and a 130-week outer limit
entries.answer: Four creation methods, and a 130-week outer limit (Core, 13 min): Automatic best method, weighted history, imported source days, or a finished short-term file.

entries.title: The editor shows history as read-only lines
keywords: the editor shows history as read-only lines
entries.answer: The editor shows history as read-only lines (Core, 11 min): Short-term granularity is 15, 30, or 60 minutes. Long-term granularity is daily or weekly.

entries.title: The schedule has to sit inside the short-term weeks
keywords: the schedule has to sit inside the short-term weeks
entries.answer: The schedule has to sit inside the short-term weeks (Advanced, 13 min): Generation offers a forecast only when those weeks cover the schedule, and only one schedule is generated at a time.

entries.title: Use the forecast, then go back to the floor
keywords: use the forecast, then go back to the floor
entries.answer: Use the forecast, then go back to the floor (Advanced, 11 min): Intraday compares the plan with what happened. Adherence is a different WFM page.

entries.title: Quality and speech analytics
synonyms: evaluation forms, ai scoring, topics and programs, and the limits on the speech-analytics articles
entries.answer: Quality and speech analytics: Evaluation forms, AI scoring, topics and programs, and the limits on the speech-analytics articles. This track has 6 lessons in this lab.

entries.title: Quality evaluates the interaction. Speech analytics reads it
keywords: quality evaluates the interaction. speech analytics reads it
entries.answer: Quality evaluates the interaction. Speech analytics reads it (Foundation, 12 min): The quality article says speech and text analytics runs on 100 percent of interactions. That is a claim to re-open, not a sample size you invent.

entries.title: A question is human, AI scored, or assisted by topics
keywords: a question is human, ai scored, or assisted by topics
entries.answer: A question is human, AI scored, or assisted by topics (Foundation, 12 min): The form article names three automation choices. Evaluation focus is Full Interaction or Evaluated Agent.

entries.title: AI scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer
keywords: ai scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer
entries.answer: AI scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer (Core, 14 min): A rolling window of 25 submissions. Below 75 percent, the answer is hidden. The transcript needs 300 characters.

entries.title: Phrases make a topic. Topics make a program
keywords: phrases make a topic. topics make a program
entries.answer: Phrases make a topic. Topics make a program (Core, 12 min): A program is mapped to queues or flows, and it can turn sentiment and empathy on or off.

entries.title: Programs have counts, and the organization switch wins
keywords: programs have counts, and the organization switch wins
entries.answer: Programs have counts, and the organization switch wins (Advanced, 14 min): One hundred programs. Five hundred topics per dialect. Twenty scoring rules. Sentiment off at the org turns it off everywhere.

entries.title: Agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation
keywords: agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation
entries.answer: Agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation (Advanced, 12 min): Each, first, or last matched agent. The article also says the last participant is the evaluated agent.

entries.title: The telephony door this lab can cite is BYOC, not a word the page did not use
keywords: the telephony door this lab can cite is byoc, not a word the page did not use
entries.answer: The telephony door this lab can cite is BYOC, not a word the page did not use (Foundation, 12 min): CPaaS is the classroom name for a communications API you bring. The opened page is About BYOC Cloud.

entries.title: Salesforce and Zendesk are the embeds this lab opened
keywords: salesforce and zendesk are the embeds this lab opened
entries.answer: Salesforce and Zendesk are the embeds this lab opened (Core, 13 min): Salesforce Open CTI is in maintenance and has a later retirement date. Zendesk’s page does not say that.

entries.title: A bot, a Virtual Agent, and Copilot are three assists
keywords: a bot, a virtual agent, and copilot are three assists
entries.answer: A bot, a Virtual Agent, and Copilot are three assists (Core, 12 min): Dialog Engine builds the bot. Virtual Agent adds Genesys AI. Copilot sits with the person.

entries.title: Future hooks are dates on announcements, not a roadmap this lab invented
keywords: future hooks are dates on announcements, not a roadmap this lab invented
entries.answer: Future hooks are dates on announcements, not a roadmap this lab invented (Advanced, 12 min): Journey Outcomes, Salesforce Open CTI, and Customer Outcomes are three different sentences.

steps.text: Signal Floor is a free operations lab. It runs in the browser and does not call a live organization. The wings below are Diagrams, Flows, Charts, Cheat Codes, and Ecosystem.
Diagrams are teaching sketches. Each caption names the limit of the drawing and links a source.
Flows are the animated pictures from the atlas, plus Mermaid drawings made at build time. The browser does not load Mermaid.
Charts count lessons, minutes, levels, quiz items, diagram kinds, and port rows in this lab. They are not production metrics.
Cheat codes are one-page sheets as HTML, PDF, and PNG, plus flashcards and an offline zip.
Ecosystem lists every track. WEM, recording, emergency calling, CRM, and bots sit on documented edges of the platform.
Foundations. What Genesys Cloud CX is, where an organization lives, and how a voice conversation is supposed to move.
Architect flows. Flow types, tasks, in-queue experiences, data actions, bots, secure calls, and publish. A draft does not answer. Publish the flow.
ACD routing. Standard, bullseye, preferred, predictive, and conditional routing, plus the two scoring methods.
Queues, skills, and wrap-up. Queue media settings, skills, wrap-up codes, callbacks, and service level.
BYOC Cloud and SIP trunks. Carrier and PBX trunks, RTP over the internet, Dynamic Cloud Voice, and the quick-start order.
Ports: TLS trunks use TCP 5061. UDP or TCP trunks commonly use 5060. Media is UDP 16384-65535. Copy live addresses from the current article, not from this lab.
Genesys AI and bots. Dialog Engine and digital bots, failure paths, Agent Copilot, tokens, and the AI exams as the catalog names them.
Speech and text analytics. What gets transcribed, how sentiment and topics are used, and why analysis is not the same thing as the live conversation.
Predictive Engagement. Website journeys, segments, action maps, Messenger, and the Journey Outcomes deprecation. This is not ACD predictive routing.
Platform APIs. OAuth grants, client credentials limits, region hosts, and why this lab’s explorer never sends a request.
AppFoundry and CRM. The marketplace, the documented Salesforce and Zendesk embeds, and OAuth migrations that do not invent other CRMs.

questions.q: All-skills matching, with no preferred agent, picks whom?
choices: The longest idle agent who has every required skill
The agent with the highest skill rating
Any agent who is On Queue
The agent who logged in last
questions.why: All-skills matching needs every required skill, then the longest idle.

questions.q: How many rings can bullseye routing use?
choices: One, then it overflows to voicemail
questions.why: The bullseye overview, as this lab cites it, allows up to five rings.

questions.q: What is one conversation-score priority point worth?
questions.why: This lab’s router treats one priority point as 60,000 ms.

questions.q: When is a preferred agent offered first?
choices: Only if they are a member and On Queue
Only if they have been idle the longest
questions.why: Preferred agents are first only if they are members and On Queue.
SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio.

questions.q: Which port do TLS trunks commonly use?
questions.why: TLS trunks use TCP 5061. UDP or TCP trunks commonly use 5060.

questions.q: What answers a call in Architect?
questions.why: Save is a draft. Publish is what answers.

choices: No. That grant has no user.
questions.why: Client credentials are for a service. The token cannot call /api/v2/users/me.
